name: Dimmer Outlet
description: An in-wall duplex outlet whose top receptacle can be dimmed and switched remotely over Insteon while the bottom receptacle stays always on. It controls plug-in lamps from Insteon keypads, remotes, or the Hub.

steps.text: Turn off the circuit breaker or remove the fuse supplying power to the outlet location.
Remove the wall plate from the outlet you are replacing, unscrew the outlet and pull it out from the junction box.
Disconnect the wires from the old outlet. If they can't be unscrewed, cut them where they enter the outlet and strip 1/2 inch of insulation off the ends.
Connect the bare copper outlet wire to the ground wire with a wire nut.
Connect the white outlet wire to the neutral wire with a wire nut.
Connect the black outlet wire to the line wire with a wire nut.
Make sure all connections are solid with no exposed copper other than ground.
Carefully install and screw the outlet into the electrical box, then install the Decora trim plate.
Turn the circuit breaker back on.
steps.expect: LED blinks red for about 1 minute, then turns solid red

steps.text: Slip the Outlet Dimmer Key over the prongs of the lamp's plug so its circular magnet faces the plug.
Plug the lamp into the top outlet.
steps.expect: The lamp turns on and the LED turns green

steps.text: If the lamp doesn't turn on, turn it on with the lamp's own switch.
Tap the SET button to check that it toggles the lamp.
steps.expect: LED is green when the lamp is on and red when it is off

notes: Neutral is required: the outlet has black (line), white (neutral) and bare copper (ground) wires.
The top outlet is dimmable and needs the Outlet Dimmer Key fitted to any plug in it; the bottom outlet is always on.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the outlet beeps.

notes: As a controller: before entering linking mode, set the responder to the state it should take when the scene is activated; after the outlet beeps, press and hold the responder's SET button until it beeps or its LED flashes. The outlet double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.

As a responder: plug a lamp fitted with the Dimmer Key into the top outlet and turn it on, press and hold the controller's scene button until it beeps, then press and hold the outlet's SET button until it double-beeps. The outlet's LED flashes once and returns to green.
Continuous beeps for 3 seconds mean an unsuccessful scene change or the 4-minute setup timeout.

verification.note: When adding the outlet to the Hub, the OutletLinc Dimmer 2472D Quick Start Guide says to hold the SET button until you hear a double-beep; the OutletLinc Dimmer 2472D Owner's Manual describes a single beep when the outlet enters linking mode itself and a double-beep when it links as a responder. The catalog uses the owner's manual's single beep.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the outlet beeps.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.

Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

The Insteon Developer's Guide (2009) says i1 devices don't support Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), and the catalog doesn't know the engine of every version of this product. An i2 or i2CS version takes it; ask the device with Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) first.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the outlet beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until the outlet beeps.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps or its LED blinks.
steps.expect: The outlet double-beeps and its LED stops blinking

notes: To remove the outlet as a responder: press and hold the controller's scene button until it beeps, press and hold it again until it beeps, then press and hold the outlet's SET button until it double-beeps. The outlet's LED flashes once and returns to steady green or red.

steps.text: If possible, remove all scene memberships first.
Turn off the circuit breaker.
Press and hold the SET button. Do not let go.
Have someone turn the circuit breaker back on while you keep holding.
When the beep stops, release the SET button.
steps.expect: The LED turns solid green and then off; after a few seconds the outlet double-beeps

steps.text: Remove the outlet from every scene controller it responds to.
Remove each responder the outlet controls that will no longer be used.
Stop using the outlet.

notes: Otherwise its controllers keep retrying commands, creating network delays.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove every link between the Hub and the device with no SET button press. First the device's group 1 link: Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) is sent to the device while the modem joins as responder. Then the modem's group 0 link: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09). This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as the OutletLinc Dimmer 2472D Owner's Manual gives it, clears them. This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.
